lessons: Checks were green and scope was fine. Review snagged on crash and replay ordering, not on missing wiring. Keep the existing wiring and fix only the write order.
author.py: append the idempotent `retro-ticket/<stem>` bridge signal BEFORE `intake.commit`. A bridge written after the commit can leave an orphan committed retro ticket that Merge blocks forever.

box.py record_rereport: build the incremented message in memory, call the callback first, then persist the count and the reopen in ONE `_replace`. Persisting reports before the callback makes the `/3` key unstable when the callback fails or the process crashes.

Fire the reopen at exactly the threshold crossing, not `>=`, so a re-tombstoned record does not reopen on its next arrival. A reviewer also flagged lifetime vs tombstone-scoped counting; state your reading in the run record.
Add tests: the callback raises once and the retry journals exactly `tombstone-reopen/<id>/3`; a bridge-append failure leaves no committed ticket; a re-tombstoned record does not reopen immediately.
triage.py semantic tombstone match: make the rereport count idempotent for each incoming message (resolve the incoming message first, or skip on retry), so replaying one arrival never counts twice.
Strengthen the constructor-coverage test: one callback per `Box(` call per file (runner.py has two), plus a Merge test that Verification/base-failure is unchanged and never reads Box provenance.
reason: Fixable write-ordering and threshold defects named by review with concrete paved roads; capability was sufficient.
